comments.author: _Algernon_
comments.story: My Coffee Maker Just Makes Coffee
comments.why: Hoffmann's french press method yields good coffee in bulk.
comments.text: I've had a lot of success with James Hoffman's method[1] for making coffee with a french press. Good coffee and with a larger french press you can make enough coffee at once for at least two people. You only need a french press and optionally a coffee grinder if you want to grind your own beans to get started. It is a bit time consuming (10-15minutes) so it may not be great for making a quick cup before leaving the house in the morning though. [1]: [VIDEO]

comments.author: code_biologist
comments.story: A scientific run-down of coffee blooming
comments.why: Cited for the 16:1 water to coffee ratio.
comments.text: Obviously immersion brewing is different than percolation, but the 16g water : 1g coffee ratio is exactly what James Hoffman recommends in his "Ultimate French Press Technique": [VIDEO] For OP's light medium roast (dark roast prefers cooler temps) Hoffman says high temps aren't a problem and shows hard boiling water lead to peak brewing temperatures of 90-93C: [LINK] Other youtubers have done blind taste tests and found they liked boiling water brews best with light roast coffee. Not saying your taste is wrong either, just that OP is doing things a way described as ideal by at least one coffee expert! Lots of ways to brew.
